title: BHHT-dual nondegenerate invertible polynomials with a cyclic parity-condition permutation group and no atomic-loop flips have reduced orbifold Milnor-fibre Euler characteristics equal up to (-1)^n
author: Wolfgang Ebeling; Sabir M. Gusein-Zade
work: Dual Invertible Polynomials with Permutation Symmetries and the Orbifold Euler Characteristic
source_version: Official SIGMA 16 (2020) article 051, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2020.051; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
difficulty_reason: The proof must synchronize fixed-point strata of nonabelian semidirect-product actions under polynomial transposition and dual annihilator subgroups. It supplies separate chain and rotated-loop calculations, an arithmetic reduction of commuting permutation pairs, and a subgroup-order comparison that includes the reduced point contribution. This combination of singularity-theoretic fixed-locus computation and finite-group duality is well beyond standard qualifying-exam Euler-characteristic or character calculations.

source_check.note: The full selected Theorem 4.1 proof and all new supporting Propositions 3.4–3.6 and 4.2–4.3 were read. The source computes fixed loci separately for atomic chains and rotated loops, reduces commuting pairs in a cyclic permutation group by the Euclidean algorithm, includes the empty-coordinate contribution for the reduced invariant, and matches subgroup orders under dual annihilators with the parity sign. Prior atomic classification, torus Milnor-fibre Euler-characteristic formula, induction invariance and established dual-group identifications are explicitly cited background. The source expressly excludes flips of atomic loops in Section 3; the selected scope retains that exclusion. A bounded source typography warning is recorded below, rather than editing author formulas. Source approval supplied only by exact frozen root input; no new source/difficulty decision or mathematical referee.

retained_original_metadata.statement_scope: Theorem 4.1 in n variables over C: f is a nondegenerate invertible polynomial, S<=S_n is cyclic, preserves f and satisfies PC (dim(C^n)^T congruent n mod 2 for every T<=S), G<=G_f is S-invariant, and the dual pair is (transpose(f), annihilator(G) semidirect S). Retain the Section 3 standing exclusion of flips of atomic loops: returns of a permutation to a loop summand act by rotations. The claim concerns REDUCED orbifold Euler characteristics of Milnor fibres; neither arbitrary permutation groups nor unreduced invariants are selected.
retained_original_metadata.editorial_warning: Editorial source notice, not an author correction: in Proposition 3.4 (PDF p.7/native lines 351–353), the displayed order of Im(A_sigma) omits the power N in its numerator. The preceding source declares |G_f|=(P^k-(-1)^(k*l))^N and |Ker(A_sigma)|=P-(-1)^l, and the closing display on p.8/native 371 explicitly gives the N-power expression and equality with |Im(A_sigma)|. The unchanged author pages retain both displays; the intended order is fixed by the same proof, without supplying a new argument. The later magnitude comparisons temporarily suppress the parity sign after explicitly explaining its common value.
